extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, analysts of calculus, and learned readers evaluating the foundations of fluxions/infinitesimals
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical and logical critique of the methods of the modern analysis (fluxions, moments, infinitesimals), focused on whether its objects, principles, and inferences are clearly conceived and legitimately deduced. The text assesses clarity, consistency, admissibility of infinitesimal reasoning, and proper logical method in mathematical demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine principles and methods with impartial freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Their Principles and Methods to be examined with the same freedom, which they assume with regard to the Principles and Mysteries of Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't allow practitioners to claim immunity from scrutiny; mathematical methods should be subjected to open, impartial examination like any other set of principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of objects (fluxions, moments, infinitesimals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moments or nascent Increments of flowing quantities difficult to conceive; Fluxions of different Orders, Second and third Fluxions obscure Mysteries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A method's fundamental concepts (e.g., fluxions, moments, infinitesimals) must be clearly conceived; if second/third orders are inconceivable, this is a sign of defective foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid presuming mathematical authority beyond competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians presumed to be the great masters of Reason, hence an unmeasured reference to their decisions where they have no right to decide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not defer to mathematical authority on topics outside demonstrable competence; acceptance by authority is not substitute for valid argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and symbols must correspond to intelligible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Deluded by their own Species or Symbols — nothing easier than to devise expressions or notations; remove the veil and consider the things themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation that is concise or regular must still represent well-defined objects; clear ontology is required beneath symbolic manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not draw conclusions from inconsistent suppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: No true Conclusion to be justly drawn by direct consequence from inconsistent Suppositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proof relies on a supposition that is later negated, consequences derived from the original supposition cannot be retained; logical consistency across steps is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove principles by principles, not by inverting logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions to be proved by Principles, and not Principles by the Conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid circular or inverted argumentation where conclusions are used to justify the very axioms or rules that produced them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject the shifting-of-hypothesis sophism (suppositio fallacia)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Shifting of the Hypothesis, or (as we may call it) the fallacia Suppositonis be not a Sophism, that far and wide infects modern reasonings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not switch from 'assume nonzero increment' to 'let increment vanish' mid-derivation: the assumption's scope must be preserved or the derivation restarted under the new hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate elimination of higher-order infinitesimals must be justified
rubrics_metrics.description: The getting rid of quantities by the received Principles, whether of Fluxions or of Differences, neither good Geometry nor good Logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dropping terms like ab or higher-order infinitesimals requires explicit justification (e.g., limit arguments); mere convenience is not proof of legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in symbolic interpretation (no double meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: I admit that Signs may be made to denote either any thing or nothing at all: and consequently that in the original Notation x + o y might have signified either an Increment or nothing. But then ... you must argue consistently with such its Signification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols must have a single, consistently applied interpretation throughout a derivation; reinterpreting a symbol midproof is a sophism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on implicit deference to authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit deference of Mathematicians for the great Author of Fluxions. Their easiness rather to go on fast and far than to set out warily and see their way distinctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usefulness or prestige of a theory's originator does not substitute for sound demonstrations or transparent principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moments cannot be finite; admitting a medium between finite and nothing admits infinitesimals
rubrics_metrics.description: If by a Momentum you mean more than the very initial Limit, it must be either a finite Quantity or an Infinitesimal. But all finite Quantities are expressly excluded from the Notion of a Momentum. Therefore the Momentum must be an Infinitesimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether 'moments' are conceived as limits, infinitesimals, or finite quantities; hidden commitments to infinitesimals should be acknowledged and defended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not suppose increments vanish while retaining expressions derived from their nonvanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is said, let the Increments vanish, i.e. let the Increments be nothing, the former Supposition that the Increments were something ... is destroyed, and yet an Expression got by virtue thereof is retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot assume increments are nonzero to derive relations, then set them to zero and keep consequences from the earlier assumption; either carry out a legitimate limiting process or rederive under the new hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluxions/velocities must be anchored to time and space measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Velocities not to be abstracted from Time and Space: Nor their Proportions to be investigated or considered exclusively of Time and Space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting fluxions as velocities, ensure they are defined in relation to an underlying measure (time/space), not as free-floating metaphysical quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptions of second/third (and higher) fluxions are suspect if inconceivable
rubrics_metrics.description: A second Fluxion seems an obscure Mystery. The incipient Celerity of an incipient Celerity ... the clear Conception of it will ... be found impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If successive derivatives are presented as new 'entities' one must show how those are intelligible and correspond to coherent limiting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series and infinite sequences of infinitesimals require scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences of various Orders, i.e. quantities infinitely less than quantities infinitely little; and infinitesimal parts of infinitesimals, ... without end or limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infinite regress of nested infinitesimals must be given clear foundational meaning (limits, convergent series) rather than being accepted by notation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols/notation must not seduce into believing metaphysical infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern Analysis supposed by themselves to extend their views even beyond infinity: Deluded by their own Species or Symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware conflating manipulations of symbols (dx, ddx, ...) with metaphysical claims about 'infinite of infinites' unless supplied with coherent definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical demonstration must respect rules of logic used in words
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Men argue in Symbols or in Words, the Rules of right Reason are still the same. Nor can it be supposed you will plead a Privilege in Mathematics to be exempt from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic or symbolic reasoning must obey the same logical standards as verbal argument; no special exemption for mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles cannot be asserted on the basis that conclusions are true
rubrics_metrics.description: The inverted way of demonstrating your Principles by your Conclusions ... is contrary to the Rules of Logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not infer the soundness of axioms or rules merely because they lead to known true results; foundations must be shown independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer finite, assignable methods where possible for geometric measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether in Geometry it may not suffice to consider assignable finite Magnitude, without concerning ourselves with Infinity? And whether it would not be righter to measure large Polygons having finite Sides, instead of Curves ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever geometric quantities can be approximated and measured by finite constructs, prefer such finite approximations to dubious infinitesimal hypotheses for purposes of measurement and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in premises (even infinitesimal) must be reflected in conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever errors are admitted in the Premises, proportional errors ought to be apprehended in the Conclusion, be they finite or infinitesimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that discarding infinitesimal errors in premises automatically yields exact conclusions; analyze error propagation and show why omitted terms don't affect final result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of quantity and divisibility require explicit metaphysical commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Geometrical Quantity hath coexistent Parts? And whether all Quantity be not in a flux as well as Time and Motion? Whether Extension can be supposed an Attribute of a Being immutable and eternal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about ontological views (coexistent parts, infinite divisibility) that underpin mathematical reasoning; hidden metaphysical assumptions can lead to paradoxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating zero/nothing as an ordinary quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the common Assumption that a finite Quantity divided by nothing is infinite be not of this Number? ... Whether the bringing Nothing under the Notion of Quantity may not have betrayed Men into false Reasoning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations involving zero (division by zero, using 'nothing' as quantity) must be prohibited or carefully redefined; treating zero as quantity invites fallacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic manipulations valid in general signs must be checked when applied to particular geometric cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether because, in stating a general Case of pure Algebra, we are at full liberty to make a Character denote, either a positive or a negative Quantity, or nothing at all, we may therefore in a geometrical Case, limited by Hypotheses ... claim the same Licence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When moving from algebraic generality to geometrical particularity, verify that the algebraic liberties taken remain valid under the specific geometric constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions/notations useful only insofar as reducible to numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Expressions in Lines or Species can be useful but so far forth as they are reducible to Numbers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols and geometrical species are instruments; their value rests on the ability to reduce them to numerical relations or clearly-interpretable measures when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confuse computational facility with being 'man of science'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Difference between a mere Computer and a Man of Science be not, that the one computes on Principles clearly conceived, and by Rules evidently demonstrated, whereas the other doth not?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to compute swiftly is not equivalent to understanding principles; favor methods that illuminate foundations over mere calculational tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematicians should examine their own principles before deriding religious mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether such Mathematicians as cry out against Mysteries, have ever examined their own Principles? ... Whether Mathematicians, who are so delicate in religious Points, are strictly scrupulous in their own Science?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage introspection: if one rejects mysteries in religion for being obscure, be consistent and scrutinize the obscurities present in one's own mathematical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of infinitesimal methods by demonstrating their logical foundations or replace with finite grounded methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same things which are now done by Infinites may not be done by finite Quantities? And whether this would not be a great Relief to the Imaginations and Understandings of Mathematical Men?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either provide solid logical foundations (limits, epsilons/deltas) for infinitesimal reasoning, or show equivalent finite methods (approximations, limits via sequences) that obviate need for problematic infinitesimals.
